name: Pong (1972)
teaser: Atari's first hit was a rejected idea — Nolan Bushnell copied table tennis after playing a Magnavox demo, and the game's 'failure to add coins' made it the first quarter-eating arcade phenomenon.

exploreAction.instruction: Play one round and notice the physics — the ball's angle is the whole game. The genius is that the simplicity is the design.

name: Space Invaders (1978)
teaser: The game that caused a Japanese coin shortage — the aliens speed up as you kill them because the CPU runs faster with fewer sprites, an accident that became the difficulty curve.

exploreAction.instruction: Play and notice the speed-up — the CPU is the game designer. The genius is that the 'invaders' march is the countdown.

name: Pac-Man (1980)
teaser: The first game with a mascot — the maze was hand-drawn as a single continuous line, and the ghosts' AI (Blinky, Pinky, Inky, Clyde) was designed so each one behaves differently.

exploreAction.instruction: Play one maze and notice the ghost personalities — each one has a real AI pattern. The genius is that the maze is a single line.

name: Donkey Kong (1981)
teaser: The game that introduced Mario (then 'Jumpman') — the barrels' physics are the game, and the 'skip screen' trick (the 22nd level kill screen) was a bug that became legend.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first level and notice the barrel physics — the timing is the game. The genius is that the jump is the whole vocabulary.

name: Super Mario Bros. (1985)
teaser: The game that saved the video game industry after the 1983 crash — the level 1-1 was designed as a tutorial that teaches you to play without a single word.

exploreAction.instruction: Play level 1-1 and notice the teaching — every hazard is introduced safely first. The genius is that the level is a lesson.

name: The Legend of Zelda (1986)
teaser: Shigeru Miyamoto designed it as a 'miniature garden' — the game famously has no linear path, and the 'it's dangerous to go alone' line is the most quoted in gaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first dungeon and notice the openness — you can go anywhere. The genius is that the exploration is the plot.

name: Metroid (1986)
teaser: The game that invented the 'Metroidvania' genre — the ending reveals the protagonist is a woman, a twist that was hidden until you finished the game.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first area and notice the locked doors — the backtracking is the design. The genius is that the reveal is the reward.

name: Final Fantasy VII (1997)
teaser: The JRPG that made the genre global — the game's famous death scene is the moment the genre grew up, and the game's budget was so large it nearly bankrupted Square.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening and notice the scale — the game is a film in 1997 terms. The genius is that the story is the combat.

name: Chrono Trigger (1995)
teaser: Developed by the 'Dream Team' (Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest and Dragon Ball creators) — the game has 13 endings and no random encounters, a radical choice in 1995.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first few hours and notice the pacing — no random battles, no filler. The genius is that the time travel is the structure.

name: Sonic the Hedgehog (1991)
teaser: Built to counter Mario — Sonic's speed was the answer to Mario's jump, and the first level's loop-the-loop was the first time a console game felt fast.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the Green Hill Zone and notice the speed — the level is a rollercoaster. The genius is that the speed is the character.

name: Street Fighter II (1991)
teaser: The fighting game that created the genre — every character had a unique move set, and the 'hadouken' became the most famous input in gaming history.

exploreAction.instruction: Play as Ryu and learn the special moves — the quarter-circle is the grammar. The genius is that the roster is the game.

name: Mortal Kombat (1992)
teaser: The game that caused the ESRB rating system — the digitized actors and fatalities were so violent that the US government held hearings on video game violence.

exploreAction.instruction: Play one match and notice the digitized realism — real actors, real motion. The genius is that the controversy IS the marketing.

name: Doom (1993)
teaser: The game that defined the FPS — the engine was written in a week, and the game's shareware model (free first episode) made it the most-installed game of its era.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first episode and notice the level design — the geometry is the combat. The genius is that the shareware was the marketing.

name: Quake (1996)
teaser: The first fully 3D FPS — the game's engine was so advanced it was licensed for decades, and the 'rocket jump' was an accident that became a skill.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first level and notice the 3D — the verticality is new. The genius is that the rocket jump is the speedrun.

name: Half-Life (1998)
teaser: The game that invented the scripted FPS — the entire story happens in real time with no cutscenes, and the opening tram ride is a tutorial disguised as a commute.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first 30 minutes and notice the scripted events — no cutscenes, all in-world. The genius is that the story is the environment.

name: Portal (2007)
teaser: Built from a student project (Narbacular Drop) — the game's 'companion cube' and GLaDOS are the most quoted AI in gaming, and the ending song was written by the writer's band.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first chambers and notice the teaching — each test is a lesson. The genius is that the puzzle is the character.

name: Counter-Strike (2000)
teaser: Born as a Half-Life mod — the game's economic system (buy rounds) became the template for tactical shooters, and its one-life-per-round tension defined esports.

exploreAction.instruction: Play a round and notice the economy — the buy system is the strategy. The genius is that the tension is the design.

name: Team Fortress 2 (2007)
teaser: The class-based shooter with nine distinct characters — the game's 'Meet the Team' videos became the standard for game marketing, and the hats became a meme economy.

exploreAction.instruction: Play as two different classes and notice the difference — the classes are the game. The genius is that the personality is the balance.

name: Minecraft (2011)
teaser: The best-selling game of all time — built from a 'cave game' prototype in a week, and the game's 'crafting table' UI was designed in a single night.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first night and notice the survival loop — dig, build, survive. The genius is that the block is the entire vocabulary.

name: Tetris (1984)
teaser: Built on a Soviet computer by a mathematician — the game's 'tetromino' shapes are the plot, and the 'Tetris effect' (seeing blocks in your sleep) is a real psychological phenomenon.

exploreAction.instruction: Play for ten minutes and notice the piece selection — the randomness is the challenge. The genius is that the geometry is the game.

name: Pokémon Red and Blue (1996)
teaser: The monster-catching RPG that became a global phenomenon — the 'MissingNo' glitch became a legend, and the game's social element (trading) was the original multiplayer.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first town and notice the design — the 'catch' is the hook. The genius is that the trading is the multiplayer.

name: GoldenEye 007 (1997)
teaser: The movie tie-in that became a legend — the four-player split-screen was a late addition that defined the console FPS, and the game's 'Oddjob' controversy was the first balance debate.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the Facility level and notice the level design — the mission is the stealth. The genius is that the multiplayer was an afterthought.

name: Super Mario 64 (1996)
teaser: The game that taught the industry how to do 3D — the camera system was invented from scratch, and the first level's opening was a crash course in 3D movement.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first level and notice the camera — the controls are the design. The genius is that the 3D is the learning.

name: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)
teaser: Considered by many the greatest game ever made — the time-travel structure (young/old Link) was a technical breakthrough, and the game's 'Z-targeting' lock-on became the 3D action standard.

exploreAction.targetName: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Play the first temple and notice the lock-on — the combat is the design. The genius is that the time travel is the structure.

name: Resident Evil (1996)
teaser: The game that invented survival horror — the 'tank controls' were a design accident, and the game's famous 'zombie dog' jump scare was a programming bug that was kept.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the mansion and notice the resource management — the ammo IS the tension. The genius is that the horror is the economy.

name: Silent Hill (1999)
teaser: The horror game that replaced monsters with psychology — the fog was a technical limitation that became the atmosphere, and the game's 'otherworld' is a descent into the protagonist's mind.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first town and notice the fog — the limitation is the design. The genius is that the horror is the psychology.

name: Metal Gear Solid (1998)
teaser: The game that made stealth a genre — the 'Psycho Mantis' boss fight (which reads your memory card) is the most famous fourth-wall break in gaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first mission and notice the stealth — the radar is the game. The genius is that the boss fights are the philosophy.

name: Halo: Combat Evolved (2001)
teaser: The game that made the Xbox — the two-weapon limit and regenerating shields became the FPS standard, and the 'flood' reveal is one of gaming's best twists.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first level and notice the shield — the health design is the game. The genius is that the 'ring' is the level.

name: Grand Theft Auto III (2001)
teaser: The game that made open worlds mainstream — the 'sandbox' design was a technical gamble, and the radio stations became the game's real soul.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first hour and notice the freedom — the city IS the game. The genius is that the radio is the character.

name: Grand Theft Auto V (2013)
teaser: The most expensive game ever made at $265M — the three-protagonist structure was the design answer to GTA IV's linearity, and the game's heist missions are the set pieces.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first heist and notice the planning — the structure is the design. The genius is that the three characters are the game's three genres.

name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011)
teaser: The game that 'you can play forever' — the 'arrow to the knee' guard line became a global meme, and the game's mod support made it a decade-long phenomenon.

exploreAction.targetName: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening and notice the freedom — the world is the game. The genius is that the mods are the longevity.

name: Fallout: New Vegas (2010)
teaser: The RPG with the most branching stories in the genre — every faction is morally gray, and the game's 'Hardcore mode' was the design answer to immersion.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first town and notice the factions — every choice has a cost. The genius is that the writing is the combat.

name: Mass Effect 2 (2010)
teaser: The game where your choices determine who lives and dies — the 'suicide mission' finale is the most famous consequence system in gaming, and the game's characters are its real draw.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the character recruitment missions — the loyalty is the mechanic. The genius is that the ending is the consequence.

name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (2015)
teaser: The RPG that redefined side quests — every contract has a moral choice, and the 'Bloody Baron' quest is considered the best-written quest in gaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the Bloody Baron quest and notice the choices — every answer has a cost. The genius is that the side quests are the story.

name: Dark Souls (2011)
teaser: The game that made difficulty a design philosophy — the 'Souls-like' genre was born here, and the game's lore is hidden in item descriptions instead of cutscenes.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the Undead Burg and notice the level design — the shortcut is the reward. The genius is that the lore is the exploration.

name: Bloodborne (2015)
teaser: The faster, more aggressive sibling of Dark Souls — the 'regain' mechanic (heal by attacking) changed the combat philosophy, and the game's Lovecraftian horror is its real setting.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first area and notice the regain — the aggression is the design. The genius is that the horror is the genre.

name: Elden Ring (2022)
teaser: The open-world Souls game with lore written by George R.R. Martin — it sold 20M+ copies and won Game of the Year, and the 'open world' is the first in the genre that respects discovery.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening area and notice the discovery — the map rewards curiosity. The genius is that the open world is the dungeon.

name: God of War (2018) (2018)
teaser: The reboot that turned a rage god into a father — the one-shot camera (no cuts) was a technical feat, and the game's real subject is parenting and legacy.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening and notice the camera — one continuous shot. The genius is that the axe is the character.

name: The Last of Us (2013)
teaser: The game that made video game stories cinematic — the 'giraffe scene' became the most discussed moment in gaming, and the game's ending is a deliberate moral test.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first hour and notice the opening — the prologue is the thesis. The genius is that the story is the gameplay.

name: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves (2009)
teaser: The game that made action set-pieces cinematic — the opening train sequence is considered the best in gaming, and the game's 'impossible' set pieces are the draw.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the train sequence and notice the set-piece design — the action IS the story. The genius is that the spectacle is the craft.

name: Red Dead Redemption 2 (2018)
teaser: The most detailed open world ever made — every NPC has a life, and the game's epilogue is a meditation on endings and honor.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening chapter and notice the detail — the world is alive. The genius is that the tragedy is the structure.

name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (2017)
teaser: The game that reinvented open worlds — you can climb anything, and the game's physics engine is a real simulation. The 'it's dangerous to go alone' tradition continues in the Glider.

exploreAction.targetName: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (2017) end-to-end
exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening plateau and notice the freedom — the physics IS the game. The genius is that the climb is the answer.

name: Super Mario Odyssey (2017)
teaser: The 3D Mario that added a companion — Cappy (the hat) is the game's mechanic and character, and the game's 'New Donk City' is the most playful level in the series.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first kingdom and notice the hat — the capture mechanic is the design. The genius is that the power-up is the character.

name: Celeste (2018)
teaser: The platformer about anxiety disguised as a mountain climb — the game's 'assist mode' was a design statement, and the story of Madeline's climb is the game's real content.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first chapter and notice the theme — the mountain is the metaphor. The genius is that the difficulty is the therapy.

name: Hollow Knight (2017)
teaser: The indie Metroidvania that defined the genre's modern era — the hand-drawn world is a single connected map, and the game's lore is buried in the world itself.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first area and notice the map — the exploration is the game. The genius is that the world is the story.

name: Undertale (2015)
teaser: The RPG where you can finish without killing anyone — the 'mercy' mechanic is the game's thesis, and the game's music was composed on a laptop by one person.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first area and notice the mercy — the pacifist path is the design. The genius is that the violence is the choice.

name: Hades (2020)
teaser: The roguelike where death is the story — the 'escape attempts' are the narrative, and the game's characters remember your failures.

exploreAction.instruction: Play your first few runs and notice the story — the deaths are the content. The genius is that the roguelike IS the narrative.

name: Stardew Valley (2016)
teaser: Built by one person over four years — the farming sim is a love letter to Harvest Moon, and the game's real content is the community of Pelican Town.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first season and notice the community — the town is the game. The genius is that the farming is the rhythm.

name: Animal Crossing: New Horizons (2020)
teaser: The game that defined the pandemic lockdown — the real-time clock and island economy made it a cultural phenomenon, and the game's design philosophy is 'no pressure, ever'.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first few days and notice the real-time — the clock is the game. The genius is that the gentleness is the design.

name: Among Us (2018)
teaser: The social deduction game that exploded during lockdown — the game's 'emergency meeting' format became a genre, and the game's simple graphics are the point.

exploreAction.instruction: Play a round and notice the social gameplay — the deduction is the game. The genius is that the simplicity is the design.

name: Fortnite (2017)
teaser: The battle royale that became a cultural platform — the building mechanic is the differentiator, and the game's live events (concerts, crossovers) made it a metaverse.

exploreAction.instruction: Play a match and notice the building — the mechanic is the game. The genius is that the live events are the culture.

name: League of Legends (2009)
teaser: The game that made esports mainstream — the 'MOBA' genre was defined by it, and the game's champion roster (160+) is the deepest character design in gaming.

exploreAction.instruction: Play a match and notice the roles — the team composition is the strategy. The genius is that the champions are the depth.

name: World of Warcraft (2004)
teaser: The MMO that made online worlds mainstream — the game's 'dance' and 'leeroy jenkins' moments became internet history, and the game's community is its real content.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the starting zone and notice the world — the community is the game. The genius is that the scale is the design.

name: StarCraft (1998)
teaser: The RTS that defined competitive gaming — the game's balance (Protoss/Zerg/Terran) is still studied, and the game made South Korean esports a national sport.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first mission and notice the factions — the asymmetry is the design. The genius is that the balance is the esport.

name: Civilization VI (2016)
teaser: The 'one more turn' game — the tech tree and district system are the design, and the game's real content is the history it teaches.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first era and notice the districts — the placement is the strategy. The genius is that the history is the content.

name: Age of Empires II (1999)
teaser: The RTS that is still played competitively 25 years later — the game's 'wololo' (conversion) meme is internet history, and the game's campaigns are history lessons.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the William Wallace campaign — it's the tutorial. The genius is that the history is the content.

name: Diablo II (2000)
teaser: The game that invented the loot ARPG genre — the 'item hunt' is the game, and the game's rune system created an economy still alive today.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first act and notice the loot — the drops are the game. The genius is that the item hunt is the depth.

name: Journey (2012)
teaser: The art game that made games 'art' — the anonymous co-op (you meet strangers without names) is the design, and the game's emotional ending is a thesis on connection.

exploreAction.instruction: Play through once without rushing — the companion is the game. The genius is that the anonymity is the design.

name: Disco Elysium (2019)
teaser: The RPG with no combat — the 'skills' are voices in your head, and the game's political dialogues are the actual gameplay.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first day and notice the skills — the internal voices are the game. The genius is that the dialogue is the combat.

name: Baldur's Gate 3 (2023)
teaser: The CRPG that won Game of the Year 2023 — the game's reactivity (every choice matters) is the design, and the game's companion romances became cultural moments.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first act and notice the choices — the dice are the tension. The genius is that the freedom is the design.

name: Cyberpunk 2077 (2020)
teaser: The game that launched broken and was fixed into a masterpiece — the 2.0 update and Phantom Liberty DLC redeemed it, and the game's world design is the best realized cyberpunk in games.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the opening act and notice the world — the city is the character. The genius is that the redemption is the story.

name: Persona 5 (2016)
teaser: The stylish JRPG about rebellious teens — the 'phantom thieves' frame is the design, and the game's calendar system (days matter) is the tension.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first palace and notice the calendar — the time is the resource. The genius is that the style is the substance.

name: Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice (2019)
teaser: The FromSoftware game that replaced rolls with parries — the 'posture' system is the design, and the game won Game of the Year 2019.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first boss and notice the posture — the parry is the game. The genius is that the duel is the design.

name: Doom Eternal (2020)
teaser: The FPS where you're the demon — the 'glory kill' and resource loop (you must kill to heal) is the design, and the game's combat is a puzzle.

exploreAction.instruction: Play the first level and notice the loop — the kills are the resources. The genius is that the aggression is the design.

name: Papers, Please (2013)
teaser: The border guard simulation — the 'glory to Arstotzka' bureaucracy is the game, and the moral choices are the real content.

exploreAction.instruction: Play your first day and notice the rules — the bureaucracy is the game. The genius is that the morality is the tension.
